findings.claim: html-css-js-final-mcq-01 repeats the debugging topic quiz decision with only the key rotated. html-css-js/dom-tooling-and-async/debugging-with-devtools-breakpoints/artifact.gift '::o2 step over::' already offers 'On the first line inside total, Not quite. That is Step into' beside 'next line' and the caller, and '::o2 step out::' keys 'returns ... to its caller'. Item 01 offers the same three outcomes and keys the Step into one. The page activity also has learners 'Press Step into to enter lineTotal'. Recall of the quiz's own option labels is enough to pick the key. The added cross-file distractor ('cannot enter a function imported from another file') is a misconception nothing in the course suggests, so it is not plausible.
findings.recommendation: Keep a band-1 debugging opener, but key a stepping or Scope decision that no debugging artifact.gift item, mastery-check item, page activity or static alternative already poses. Check candidates against the page's step-in/step-out static alternative and the conditional-breakpoint activity before keying.

findings.claim: html-css-js-final-mcq-03's keyed decision is already practised three times. The cookies page Activity 1 ('Predict what injected script can read': token in localStorage versus HttpOnly cookie), the topic quiz '::o1 script access::' and the fetch mastery item 'cookies-vs-localstorage ... o1 what the attacker reads' all key 'script reads localStorage; the HttpOnly cookie value stays hidden'. Item 03's key ('The script can read the copy in localStorage') follows straight from that. Its fourth distractor ('can read the cookie through document.cookie, but localStorage stays private', feedback 'It is the other way round') is the mastery item's distractor 'Read the cookie but not localStorage' ('It is the reverse'). The token-copy twist only means the practised answer applies to the copy.
findings.recommendation: Replace the reused distractor, and move the keyed decision past 'which store can script read'. For example, ask what the copy changes about the cookie attributes' value, or what the copy makes necessary when the session ends. Use only behaviour the cookies page teaches, and check it against its four activities, five quiz items and the two fetch mastery cookie items.

findings.claim: html-css-js-final-mcq-12 repeats the semantic-html topic quiz instead of stepping up. Its outline h1, h2, then h4 with the fix 'change the h4 to an h3' is the keyed decision of html-css-js/html-and-css/semantic-html-page-structure/artifact.gift '::o2 skipped level::' (h1 Garden guide, h2 Vegetables, h4 Tomatoes; key 'should be an h3'). Its distractor 'render it at h3 size' reuses that quiz's distractor 'h4 makes the heading smaller' ('the number is a level ... not a font size'). The 'keep the class so the look is unchanged' half is the same quiz's '::o3 keep the layout::', and the aside-h2 point is the page's 'Going back up, any jump is fine'. The item merges two quiz items, which the coverage plan's difficultyRule forbids, and it is band 1 at position 12.
findings.recommendation: Replace it with a semantic-structure decision in a context no semantic artifact.gift item, html-and-css mastery item, page activity or Course Review page-and-language Activity 1 uses. The heading skip, the class-keeps-layout point and the header/main wrapping are all taken. Grep the page for any element or rule before keying it.

findings.claim: html-css-js-final-mcq-16 is Course Review Activity 2 (html-css-js/html-css-js-course-review/html-css-js-review-page-and-language/artifact.html, 'Fix the book grid on a phone') with border-box applied. That activity has a phone width, a card with width 100%, padding and border, the content-box sum 358 + 16 + 16 + 3 + 3 = 396 px, and the fix box-sizing: border-box, which its feedback says makes 'the 358 px include padding and border'. Item 16 asks the width once border-box is set: the column width, 368 px. Its main distractor, 396 px, is the content-box sum that this activity and the box-model quiz '::o2 content-box width::' / '::o2 border-box width::' drill. The Course Review's own feedback gives the answer, and item 10 already gives the box model one calculation item.
findings.recommendation: Replace item 16, keeping the bank at 30, with a box-model or responsive decision that the box-model page, quiz, mastery items and Course Review A2 do not already resolve. For example, a responsive-mobile-first objective (viewport meta, query order or overflow fix) set in a new context, after checking it against that page's activities and quiz.

findings.claim: html-css-js-final-mcq-17 merges four practised decisions and adds none: typeof null is 'object' (javascript-for-java-developers quiz '::o2 surprising typeof::' and mastery item 'javascript-for-java-developers o2 two surprising answers'), Array.isArray (quiz '::o2 detecting an array::'), mutating a const object versus reassigning it (let-const page Activity 1 and quiz '::o2 const object::'), and earlier lines running before a run-time TypeError (quiz '::o3 reading a crash::'). Each distractor's feedback restates one of those quiz keys, so recalling the quizzes is enough to pick the key. The const half is also item 29's keyed decision. This is the same ground on which item 12 is graded high.
findings.recommendation: Replace it with a JavaScript-for-Java-developers decision that none of the javascript-fundamentals quiz, mastery or page items already key. typeof null has been asked twice, and the const binding is item 29's key. Keep the listing to 6 lines or fewer, and confirm every option in a Node.js 24 run.

findings.claim: html-css-js-final-mcq-20 repeats taught decisions, and the option shapes cue the key. The stem's 'The client checks res.ok and the content-type first' is the key of Course Review Activity 3 (html-css-js/html-css-js-course-review/html-css-js-review-browser-client/artifact.html) and of the handling-http-errors page Activity 3 (problem+json, then 'Server error' for 404/502). Cases (1) and (3) are that key again, and the gateway HTML is page Activity 5. Case (2), giving a 5xx a generic message rather than its detail, is the page's own 'Choose something else when: A 5xx response ... show a generic message'. No distractor differs from the key on case (2) alone. The three distractors are blanket rules ('every error response', 'error bodies are never read', 'All three reject'), so the only option that treats the cases separately is the key, and handling (1) and (3) as practised is enough to choose it. The second distractor, which parses the HTML 404 as JSON while ignoring problem details, is not a plausible learner error.
findings.recommendation: Replace it with an error-handling decision that the http-errors page activities, quiz, mastery item 'two broken mornings' and Course Review A3 have not resolved. Write each distractor as a per-case plan that is wrong on exactly one case, so the options share the key's shape.

findings.claim: html-css-js-final-mcq-22 repeats the CORS page and quiz, and its stem cues the key. The setup (Vite page, Spring Boot on another port, plain GET, CORS error although the server answered 200) is CORS page Activity 1 ('Your page runs at http://localhost:5173, and calls http://localhost:8080/api/books with a plain GET ... The console shows a CORS error') and quiz '::o3 reading the evidence::' ('Server logs show a plain GET handled with status 200, yet the browser console shows a CORS error'; key 'the browser blocked your code from reading the response'). The fix half is page Activities 3 and 4 (Vite server.proxy with relative /api paths) and mastery item 'fixing-cors ... o2 two setups'. The mode: "no-cors" distractor and its feedback come from Activity 5's option C. The stem also states 'The team wants relative /api paths in development ... with no server CORS setup', and only the key repeats 'relative /api paths'.
findings.recommendation: Delete the requirement sentence from the stem, and key a CORS or proxy decision that the page's five activities, the five quiz items and the three fetch mastery CORS items do not already pose, preferably one that links to environment-settings (the API address) or to calling-your-spring-boot-api.

findings.claim: html-css-js-final-mcq-26 repeats a page activity almost line for line. The fetching-data page (html-css-js/fetch-and-browser-client/fetching-data/artifact.html, activity 'Why is it undefined?') shows async function loadUser() { const res = await fetch("/api/user"); const user = res.json(); console.log(user.name); } with the key 'res.json() returns a promise ... It needs await'. Item 26 is the same function with forEach instead of .name and the same keyed fix, const users = await res.json(). The fetching-data quiz '::o1 two steps::' and mastery item 'async-and-await o3 the missing await' drill the same misconception. As a band-1 item at position 26, it also breaks the easier-to-harder order.
findings.recommendation: Replace it with a fetch or await decision that no fetching-data or async-and-await quiz, mastery or page item poses. '::o1 body once::' (a second res.json()) and the try/await activity 'why was nothing caught?' are already taken. Grep both pages for every API used before keying.

findings.claim: html-css-js-final-mcq-28 merges practised facts, and its first half tests nothing. All four options begin with the same fix, 'Write count + 1n;', and the stem already says line 4 stops with a TypeError, which is the quiz fact '::o1 mixing number types::' (5n + 2). The options differ only in the printed values. 3 == "3" is true is let-const page Activity 3, quiz '::o3 loose result::' and Course Review page-and-language Activity 3's 2 == "2". Node printing BigInts with a trailing n is in the javascript-for-java-developers page activity ('ending in 616n'). count + 1n leaving count unchanged is trivial. Recalling those practised items is enough to pick the key.
findings.recommendation: Replace it with a decision about equality or number types that no let-const, javascript-for-java-developers or Course Review item keys. If a two-part 'fix and output' form is kept, the options must differ on the fix as well as on the output.

findings.claim: html-css-js-final-mcq-29 is the let-const page's Activity 2 (html-css-js/javascript-fundamentals/let-const-and-equals/artifact.html, 'Choose const or let': fill each ___ with const or let, where a constant, an accumulator and an object whose property changes give const, let, const). Item 29 asks the same task with the same categories: total +=, an object whose property changes, a loop index and a never-reassigned string. Its distractors' feedback restates quiz keys '::o1 choosing a keyword::' (loop counter, let) and '::o1 const by default::' (mutated but never reassigned, const). Its keyed decision, 'settings is only changed, not reassigned', is item 17's key, which goes against the coverage plan's 'no two items share a keyed objective'. It is the easiest item in the bank, yet it sits at position 29.
findings.recommendation: Replace item 29, keeping the bank at 30, and spend the slot on the thin promises topic (see hcj-gift-edu-12) with a decision that the promises quiz and mastery items do not key. 'return in then', 'thrown in then', Promise.all result order and 'one bad report' are all taken.

findings.claim: Items are not delivered easier to harder, which the blueprint instructions promise learners ('run from easier to harder') and the owner intent requires. Banding each item as 1 (one recall or one-step trace), 2 (two linked steps) or 3 (multi-step calculation or multi-concept diagnosis): html-css-js-final-mcq-04 (await plus a long task on the event loop, band 3) and html-css-js-final-mcq-05 (flex-shrink weighted by basis, band 3; the course only practises flex-grow sharing in its quiz and mastery items) sit at positions 4 and 5. Items 12, 19, 26 and 29 are band 1 at positions 12, 19, 26 and 29. The final third (21 to 30) holds two band-1 items and only one band-3 item (24). The heaviest items, 18 and 20 (multi-concept fetch diagnosis), sit mid-test.
findings.recommendation: After the replacements, re-band the whole bank and re-sequence it: open with the band-1 items, and move 04, 05, 18, 24 and any band-3 replacements into the last third. Record the order rationale on the private route.

findings.claim: The bank's weight is uneven. destructuring-and-spread decides four keys (06, 18, 23 and 24), and 'spread is shallow' is the keyed idea of both 06 (next.panel is the same object) and 18 (the caller's headers replace the defaults). That idea is already practised in the destructuring quiz '::o3 shallow::', the javascript-fundamentals mastery item 'destructuring-and-spread o3 the safe copy' and Course Review page-and-language Activity 3. let-const-and-equals keys three items (17, 28 and 29). In contrast, the promises topic gets no then-chain or Promise.all decision: item 25's key turns on a .catch handler on a rejected promise from an async function, and item 30 mentions Promise.all only in feedback. promises o2 (then return/throw) and o3 (Promise.all) are not reached by any key (html-css-js/dom-tooling-and-async/promises/artifact.gift).
findings.recommendation: Keep one shallow-spread item. Item 18 is the better step up, because it ties spread to fetch headers and the 415 status. Rekey item 06 on a Vitest toBe/toEqual decision that is not a shared nested object. Use a freed slot (from 17, 28 or 29) for a promises then-chain or Promise.all decision that the promises quiz and the dom-tooling mastery items do not already key.

findings.claim: html-css-js-final-mcq-04's key and feedback go against the course's model. The key says 'the loop after it is one long task', and the feedback says 'Code after an await resumes as a task on the single main thread'. Course Review browser-client teaches 'Calling an async function runs it up to its first await; the rest waits as a microtask', and the-event-loop page teaches the task and microtask queues. A learner who learned it correctly is contradicted at the final. The first distractor ('Putting await in front of the loop's function call') also refers to a function call the stem never shows, because the stem says only that the handler 'loops over a large array'.
findings.recommendation: Reword the key and the feedback: after the await, the rest of the handler resumes as a microtask on the one main thread, and its long synchronous loop holds that thread until it ends, so queued clicks wait. Either show the loop as a named call in the stem, or reword the first distractor so it matches what the stem shows.

findings.claim: In html-css-js-final-mcq-21, two of the three distractors are contradicted by the stem's own log. The stem says the Help link is 'announced by its aria-label "Help"', so the distractors claiming the link 'needs visible text to be announced' or 'needs a label element' can be ruled out from the stem without any accessibility knowledge. The key also repeats the stem's wording ('Tab reaches it but keys do nothing').
findings.recommendation: Log neutral observations and leave the learner to judge them. For example, state only that the Help link is an icon-only a element with aria-label="Help", and give the slider a symptom the learner must interpret rather than one the key restates.

findings.claim: html-css-js-final-mcq-19: 'the API contract fixes that status' is unclear for a novice whose first language may not be English, because 'fixes' can be read as 'repairs' rather than 'sets'. As a band-1 item at position 19, it is also part of the progression problem in hcj-gift-edu-11.
findings.recommendation: Write 'and the API is specified to answer 400 for it', and move the item into the first third.
